author: Tom George
title: Durham school families seek answers as repeated threats trigger lockdowns - NewsBreak
text:
By Tom George ,
45 minutes ago
Parents and students at Riverside High School met with Durham Public Schools Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis on Thursday night, seeking answers after a series of lockdowns that have disrupted learning and raised concerns about safety on campus.
School officials said Riverside has experienced 14 lockdowns, more than any other school in the district. District leaders said they believe the incidents are likely tied to the same person repeatedly abusing an anonymous tip line.
Students said the repeated lockdowns have created fear and uncertainty throughout the school.
"It's really scary honestly cause you never know when it's a real one, when it's a fake one," said Kenya Laney, Riverside's senior class president.
Laney said the lockdowns have taken an emotional toll on students.
"So, now you're imagining a scared kid in a classroom, not knowing anything that's going on. Is there an intruder outside? And then the police people are coming into our classroom. It's really stressful," she said.
Riverside sophomore Jarin Luster said students have grown frustrated by the recurring incidents.
"It's just like here we go again and since we don't know what's going on and during the lockdown, we wait for a news report or our parents send us a screenshot of what's going on," Luster said.
Parents also described the stress of being away from their children during lockdowns.
"But it's a lot. It's the stress and untoward, unwarranted stress that we're dealing with. And, you try to keep your kids calm in a situation like that. We tell them what to do, what to look out for, as well as the school. But as a parent, you're not there to protect them. Just hold on and make sure that they do the right thing," said parent Jacinta Luster.
During the meeting, parents and students shared their frustrations with Lewis, who acknowledged the impact the lockdowns have had on the school community.
"Since this is definitely impacting students and academics, it's taking an emotional toll on our students and staff in this building, and it's preventing us from providing a world class education to our scholars. So, absolutely, we want this to stop," Lewis said.
District officials said the threats have followed a similar pattern.
"Threats of an individual, they pretty much describe what the individual has on, their ethnicity, and that they were seen leaving a restroom with a gun," Lewis said.
The district said it is working with federal investigators to track IP addresses and potential virtual private networks, or VPNs, that may be masking the person's identity.
Officials said they must continue treating every threat seriously while also trying to limit disruptions to classroom instruction.
"So again, anytime a tip comes in and our law enforcement partners suggested we go into lockdown, we will continue to to do that, to keep our students and staff safe," Lewis said.
The investigation is being led by the Durham County Sheriff's Office. School officials said anyone identified as responsible could face at least 20 felony charges.
In the meantime, students said they simply want a return to normalcy.
"And really just figuring out what's going on and finishing it so every student can go on with school like it should be," Laney said.
